name: Returning to the hiring tab starts the run again and says so on the page, instead of the run staying dead until a reload
request: Returning to the hiring tab starts the run again and says so on the page, instead of the run staying dead until a reload
checks: npm run check passed (typecheck, build, 412 tests, validate)
result: Switching back to the hiring tab now restarts the run and the page says so. THE GAP: every watcher on this page asks 'did we arrive somewhere new', and applicantsViewKey is deliberately built so that opening a row does not count - but a tab switch changes no address at all, so that test could never fire for it, and nothing else was watching. Meanwhile a run interrupted by the tab going hidden gives up for good once VISIBILITY_WAIT_MS (5 min) passes. Together: glance at another window for five minutes, come back, and the surface has quietly decided the run was over - which is 'it automatically stops working', and why reloading was the only cure, a reload being the one thing that re-injects this script with a fresh state. noteReturnToTab() records the current view as a pending arrival when the tab becomes visible with no run in flight, and pumpAutoRun fulfils it through the existing bounded, retryable path. No guard rail moved: the worker is still asked whether this job was armed by the recruiter's own Collect Every Applicant, a Stop still latches disabled and refuses, and a run already in flight is left alone to continue in place rather than being restarted. showPageNotice() puts one inert line on the page - fixed, pointer-events:none so it can never come between the recruiter and a control, role=status with a polite live region, self-removing, styled inline because a content script has no stylesheet on linkedin.com and MV3's script-src CSP does not constrain the style property. It is shown at exactly the two points where work actually resumes: after waitForVisibleAgain returns true inside the run loop, and in startAutoRun after the job is known to be armed - never on a bail, because a banner saying resumed over a surface that then does nothing is worse than none. Re-injection clears the timer and removes the element so a banner is never stranded. It is not a control and nothing clicks it: the budget is still seven.
